title: Locked AI model simulates the VESALIUS-CV trial before its results were public
summary: A semi-mechanistic machine learning model combining real-world patient data with knowledge-graph drug representations simulated the evolocumab versus placebo VESALIUS-CV trial using a locked model and prespecified design. It predicted a major adverse cardiovascular event hazard ratio of 0.78 (95% CI 0.70-0.87) at 54 months; the trial later reported 0.75 (0.65-0.86). Retrospectively, patient-level time-dependent AUC was 0.80-0.90 and trial-level accuracy across 22 trials was 0.91. This is a preprint with one prospective trial and the exact architecture is not stated in the abstract.
ai_technology: Semi-mechanistic machine learning combining real-world data and knowledge-graph drug embeddings to predict time-to-event outcomes and simulate virtual trial arms
organization: Not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: Prospective locked-model simulation compared with the later published trial result, plus retrospective patient-level and 22-trial evaluation.
